title: composeStacks objectConflict misses objects declared inside nested package bodies
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaAUev5V62cLHhQwBi

Filing category: ① product defect (found in the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review of PR #32475 for #32335, comment 6809232138; read from the code, not run).
Refs #32335 · Refs #31527 (ADR-0150 D4)

## Business reason

`composeStacks` with `objectConflict: 'error'` is meant to refuse two inputs that declare the same object. A nested multi-package artifact (one `composeStacks` built under `manifest: 'preserve'`, which carries its objects only inside `packages[]` bodies) slips past that check, so two packages that both declare object `X` compose, and at boot one body's `X` silently replaces the other.

## What happens

1. `mergeObjects` in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` walks each input's top-level `objects` only.
2. A stripped nested artifact whose `packages[K]` body declares object `X`, composed beside an input that also declares `X`, therefore passes under `objectConflict: 'error'`. The same pair as flat inputs is refused.
3. After #32335 (PR #32475), step 6 reads the action keys of package bodies, but it skips a body's object-embedded actions on the premise that the object door has already judged that object. So an `X:approve` embedded on both sides is admitted too.

## Expected

The object door judges the objects that `packages[]` bodies declare as it judges top-level ones: `objectConflict: 'error'` refuses the nested + flat pair exactly as it refuses the flat pair.

Re-check (premise): `git grep -n "function mergeObjects" -- packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, then read whether it reads `packages[].objects`.
Reader who acts: the seat that owns `composeStacks` (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`); a refusal added at compose is a narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, contract-tier review).
